case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation
- Pier fishing for salmon looks slow at all four ports. Rough ratings: Grand Haven 1, St. Joseph 1, South Haven 1 (the report says "slow"), Muskegon not rated (no pier report).
- Go to the Grand Haven pier. Start with alewife or orange spoons for the few coho that are being caught.
- If the pier stays slow, consider a boat. Boat fishing has been rated good at Grand Haven and Muskegon.

## Why
- Grand Haven is the only one of the four with a pier report that names lures working on the pier (alewife or orange spoons) (Grand Haven, 2026-05-18 — see the year note below).
- Every pier report from the last six weeks is rated 0 or 1, so none of these ports has shown good pier fishing this spring (all four ports, April to May 2022).
- Boats at Grand Haven and Muskegon were rated good on May 18, so a boat is the better bet if the pier is slow (Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2022-05-18).
- I'd expect pier fishing to stay around average-to-slow this week, because the newest pier report is six days old and no pier report has shown a clear bite yet.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (latest is 2022-05-18, six days old)
- Grand Haven pier: "Pier anglers were catching a few coho salmon on alewives or while casting orange spoons." Quality 1 (2022-05-18).
- St. Joseph pier: "Anglers were also catching an occasional coho… spawn was catching the coho." Quality 1 (2022-05-18).
- South Haven pier: "Pier fishing remained slow but there was an occasional coho caught on spawn." Quality 1 (2022-05-18).
- Muskegon: no pier report in the last six weeks. Its only report is for boats: "Boats were doing well catching salmon 35 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water." Quality 3 (2022-05-18).
- Earlier pier reports were also slow: Grand Haven "slow" (2022-04-27), South Haven "very slow" (2022-04-20), St. Joseph "slow" (2022-04-20).

**Past seasons**
- I searched for earlier seasons with similar water (about 53 F within 21 days of May 24). The only matches were the same May 18 reports, so I have no older comparison for this week.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water (measured, offshore): about 53 F at St. Joseph and South Haven and about 52 F at Grand Haven and Muskegon. Each dropped 3–4 F over the week before May 24 (buoy summary for the week before 2022-05-24).
- No modeled pierhead water temperature was available in this check, so I can't tell whether the pier water is cooling.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old, and the season is moving fast. Treat these ratings as a guide.
- Muskegon has no pier report, so its rating is missing rather than low.
- Current conditions came from the offshore buoy only. The buoy drop may point to upwelling, which can bring salmon to piers, but I can't confirm that at the piers.
- Report year note: the bulletins are dated 2022, which matches today's date.

## Sources
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph, week of May 18: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- May 4: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
- April 27: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3155afc
- April 20: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3145666
